candidates.title: Temperature-adjust RLHF policy probabilities before trusting confidence
candidates.rule: Do not read confidence directly off an RLHF-finetuned policy's output distribution; apply a single global temperature rescaling (one constant fitted across tasks) before using its probabilities as calibrated confidence.
candidates.passage: a simple temperature adjustment (with the same temperature T = 2.5 for all evaluations) largely fixes calibration issues with several independent evaluation tasks
candidates.finding: Helpful-and-harmless RLHF policies finetuned from the same base LMs appeared badly miscalibrated on multiple-choice evaluations; a single temperature of 2.5 shared across three evaluations largely restored calibration. The authors note more intensive RL training might distort calibration beyond what temperature can fix.
models: RLHF policies finetuned from Anthropic base LMs (trained as in Bai et al., 2022)
workloads: three multiple-choice evaluations (not individually specified in the quoted result)
candidates.conditions: Requires access to output token probabilities; the constant T=2.5 is specific to these policies and evaluations and must be refit per model.
candidates.limitations: Brief side experiment, few evaluations, single paper. T=2.5 is not transferable; heavier RL or different reward models may produce distortions temperature cannot correct. Does not address calibration of free-form verbal confidence.
candidates.validation_test: For an RLHF model with logprob access, measure ECE on several multiple-choice sets before and after fitting one global temperature on a held-out set, and check whether a single constant generalizes across the tasks.

reason: The paper contains several directly tested prompt/format interventions with measured effects on calibration and self-evaluation quality, which map to actionable harness rules. I propose three distinct ones: lettered single-token multiple-choice formatting (and avoiding 'none of the above'), few-shot True/False self-evaluation with multiple sampled candidates as a filter, and temperature adjustment for RLHF-policy confidence. All are from a single 2022 Anthropic paper on 800M-52B internal models, so transfer is uncertain.
